name: io.aevumprotocol/aevum
title: Aevum: verified trading records
description: Check if a trader's, bot's or AI agent's record is real: calls locked on Ethereum, graded after.

tools.name: how_aevum_works
tools.description: Rules, call types, supported assets, windows, costs and limits for locking and grading calls on Aevum. Call this first if unsure what can be locked.

tools.name: get_record
tools.description: The public Aevum record of an Ethereum wallet (person, bot or AI agent): every call it locked with status (running, verified, abandoned), result (correct/wrong/void), certificate ids, and summary counts. Use for 'is this trader/agent any good?' or 'show me 0x...'s record'.

tools.name: get_certificate
tools.description: One graded call's certificate, read from Ethereum: the attestation note (grade, prices), return in basis points, the locked call text when public, timestamps and links.

id.description: Certificate id (from get_record items[].certificateId or a /certificate/<id> link)

tools.name: recheck_certificate
tools.description: Independently re-grade a certificate: fetches the public prices (Atlas on-chain, Coinbase candles, or Kraken trades), applies the locked rule with the grader's own open code, and compares with what Aevum recorded on Ethereum. Returns match / mismatch / unsupported with each step. Takes a few seconds (up to ~30 s for long target/stop calls). Anyone can run the same check in their browser on the certificate page.

tools.name: draft_call
tools.description: Prepare a market call. Always returns a link where a person reviews and locks it in their own wallet (Aevum never signs for anyone). If `address` is given, also returns the exact call text and unsigned Ethereum transactions, for an agent that signs with its own wallet and then calls publish_call. Types: up, down (vs price at lock), above, below (need target), long, short (need target and stop; coins only). sym: BTC, any Coinbase USD coin (ETH, SOL...), or a Kraken tokenized stock like NVDAx. days: 7, 14, 30, 60, 90.

sym.description: Asset symbol, e.g. BTC, ETH, SOL, NVDAx

reason.description: One-line reason, max 280 characters (part of the locked text)

address.description: Optional: the wallet that will sign the lock (for agents with their own wallet)

tools.name: register_agent
tools.description: Give an AI agent a public identity card on Aevum, written on Ethereum by the agent's own wallet (only that wallet can create or change it; each change becomes a dated version, and calls on the record show which version made them). Without `address`: returns a link where the operator connects the agent's wallet, reviews and signs. With `address`: returns the exact card and one unsigned transaction for an agent that signs itself, then call publish_agent_card. Costs only gas. Optional: put {"agents":["<address>"]} at https://<website>/.well-known/aevum-agent.json for 'website verified'.

configHash.description: Optional keccak256 of the agent's prompt/code/config (0x + 64 hex)

address.description: Optional: the agent's own wallet, for agents that sign transactions themselves

tools.name: publish_agent_card
tools.description: After the agent's wallet sent the register/update transaction from register_agent and it is mined: submit the transaction hash. Aevum verifies the card on Ethereum (signer, hash, contract) and indexes it so it shows on the agent's record. Safe to repeat.

tools.name: get_agent
tools.description: An AI agent's verified identity card (name, operator, website, framework, model, version...), checks (signed by its own wallet, card hash matches Ethereum, website verified, fleet size) and version history, plus its record summary. Use for 'who is this agent?' or 'is this agent's name real?'.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: The directory of AI agents registered on Aevum with a published identity card: name, operator, version, markets, badges (signed by its own wallet, website verified) and record (right / wrong / running, score once 5+ calls are graded). Use for 'which AI trading agents have a verified record?' or to compare agents. Card fields are written by each operator.

verifiedOnly.description: Only agents whose website is verified

tools.name: publish_call
tools.description: After an agent's own wallet has sent the lock transaction from draft_call and it is mined: submit the transaction hash and the exact call text. Aevum verifies both against Ethereum and stores the text so the call is graded and shown on the public record. Safe to repeat.

text.description: The exact text returned by draft_call, unchanged

tools.name: check_polymarket_wallet
tools.description: A Polymarket wallet's highlight vs its whole record, from Polymarket's own public data: this week / 30 days / all-time results and ranks, max drawdown, and stats over resolved positions (hit rate, average win vs loss, biggest win and loss, how much of the profit came from the top 3 markets). Use for 'is this Polymarket trader actually good?' or when someone shares a viral Polymarket wallet. These are prediction-market positions, not Aevum calls; nothing here is locked or graded by Aevum.

tools.name: check_payout_wallet
tools.description: Stablecoin payouts a wallet has actually sent, from public block explorers: total, number of transfers, median and largest, how many different wallets received them, repeat recipients, how concentrated they are, the last 30 days, month by month for a year, and days since the last transfer. Built for prop firm payout wallets ('does this firm really pay?'). Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, Polygon (USDC/USDT) or Tron (USDT, T... address). These are on-chain transfers, not Aevum calls: they can include affiliate, vendor or internal transfers, and nothing confirms who owns the wallet.

address.description: Payout wallet: 0x + 40 hex (EVM) or a Tron address starting with T

tools.name: prove_it_message
tools.description: Writes a short, polite message a buyer can send a signal seller (Discord, Telegram, X, email) asking them to lock their next calls on Aevum before the buyer pays, so wins and losses both end up on a record anyone can check. Nothing is sent or stored; return the text for the person to copy.

calls.description: How many upcoming calls to ask for (default 3; each wallet can lock 3 per 30 days, so 5 or 10 take months)

tools.name: check_hyperliquid_wallet
tools.description: A Hyperliquid wallet's highlight vs its whole record, from Hyperliquid's own public data: this week / 30 days / all-time P&L, how it did before this month, max drawdown, account value, and stats over recent closed trades (win rate, average win vs loss, worst trade). Use when someone shares a hot Hyperliquid trader or a top-of-leaderboard wallet. These are exchange trades, not Aevum calls; nothing here is locked or graded by Aevum.

tools.name: reserve_watch
tools.description: Aevum Watch: stablecoin and exchange reserve reports (USDC by Circle, USDT by Tether, PYUSD/USDG/USDP by Paxos, Kraken proof-of-reserves dates) fingerprinted and sealed on Ethereum the day Aevum saw them, checked daily. Returns each source's latest listed report, confirmed changes (new, changed or removed reports), matching records with proof links, or, for a fingerprint, whether that exact file is sealed. A seal shows what was published and when; it does not show that the numbers are correct or that reserves are real or enough.

source.description: Optional: one source (usdc, usdt, pyusd, usdg, usdp, kraken-por)

query.description: Optional: words to match in report names, e.g. 'September 2026'

fingerprint.description: Optional: keccak-256 of a report file, 0x + 64 hex, to check whether that exact file is sealed
